profile.name: Nadia Rahman
profile.intro: I design the systems, stories, and learning experiences that help people do better work.

experience.title: Head of Learning Operations
experience.description: Built the operating model for a distributed learning team: portfolio planning, vendor governance, learner insight loops, and a measurement practice that connected learning to business outcomes.

experience.title: Learning Experience Lead
experience.description: Led a cross-functional team creating blended programs for 12,000+ professionals. Introduced a reusable design system and cut time-to-launch by 35%.

experience.title: Instructional Designer
experience.description: Translated subject-matter expertise into active, accessible digital learning for a fast-growing education platform.

work.title: The learning operating system
work.summary: A practical blueprint for making learning visible, findable, and useful across a 600-person organization.
work.detail: We mapped every learning touchpoint — from onboarding to leadership development — and redesigned the underlying operating model. The result was a single intake process, a shared measurement framework, and a team that finally felt coherent.
work.challenge: Learning was fragmented across six tools, three teams, and two business units with no shared language or measurement.
work.approach: Stakeholder interviews → service blueprint → operating model design → phased rollout with embedded champions.

work.title: From content library to practice lab
work.summary: A cohort-based academy that helped new managers move from knowing the model to using it in the room.
work.detail: Instead of building more content, we built a practice environment. Small cohorts, real scenarios, peer reflection, and manager check-ins at weeks three and six.
work.challenge: Completion rates for self-paced manager training hovered at 23%. The content was sound — the format wasn't.
work.approach: Learning audit → cohort design → facilitation guide → measurement framework → facilitator certification.

work.title: A calmer tech stack
work.summary: A vendor and platform rationalization that gave learners one coherent front door to development.
work.detail: Eleven tools. Four overlapping platforms. Zero integration. We ran a vendor audit, defined a capability map, and negotiated a 28% cost reduction while improving the learner experience.
work.challenge: Rapid EdTech adoption had created a fragmented ecosystem that nobody could navigate — learners or L&D teams.
work.approach: Vendor audit → capability mapping → platform consolidation → change campaign → launch with embedded guides.

principles.title: Make the invisible visible
principles.text: Good operations create the conditions for good learning — and make the value legible to everyone.

principles.title: Design for the next action
principles.text: Learning sticks when it connects to a real decision, conversation, or behavior.

principles.title: Leave things clearer
principles.text: Every experience should reduce cognitive load, build confidence, and open a next step.

testimonials.quote: Nadia doesn't just design learning — she designs the system around learning. Everything gets better when she's involved.

testimonials.quote: She has a rare ability to see both the learner experience and the operational reality at the same time. That combination is very hard to find.
testimonials.name: Tobias Vree

testimonials.quote: The management academy she built is still the program I point to when people ask what great L&D looks like in practice.
